26.1.2612.0.8-android.28:
The performance release the last log pointed at: the section arena now grows to what the render distance actually asks for, and the threads this renderer owns run on the fast cores.

- **The arena grows again.** A render-distance report that arrived while the arena already held sections was supposed to grow it by appending another buffer, but the request was clamped to the size of a *single* buffer first - and on devices whose storage-binding limit makes one buffer smaller than the view (every Adreno at 12 chunks and up), the clamp left the request equal to what the arena already held, no growth was ever asked for, and sections the arena could not take were meshed by Minecraft's own path instead - the slower vertex format, drawn through the same GPU. The report is now clamped to the *pool's* ceiling (all buffers, under the memory budget), so a 12-chunk view gets the 192 MB it asks for across two buffers, and the sections that were falling back come back to the fast path.
- **Fragmentation now asks for room before it costs a section.** The growth trigger read how many slots were free; a churned arena holds its free slots as holes between held sections, so an arena at 39% held was refusing sections whose geometry had nowhere to sit - your log showed 909 of them. The trigger now also reads the longest *contiguous* free run, and appends a buffer while no run can take the largest section meshed so far. The refuse-then-re-mesh churn that shape produced is gone.
- **The render thread and the bake pool run on the performance cores.** On a big.LITTLE phone the scheduler parks whatever looks less busy on the slow cluster; the render thread now pins itself to the fast cores once, and the section-bake pool runs one thread per fast core, pinned there, leaving the efficiency cluster to the JVM's own background threads. Cluster detection is read from the device at runtime (cpufreq), and a device it cannot read keeps the old behaviour exactly.

If terrain ever goes missing after this build, that is a bug and not a culling choice - send the log. Nothing in this release changes what is drawn, only who meshes it and where it runs.

26.1.2612.0.8-android.29:
The batching release: the terrain draws in batches again on every device, including the one whose driver broke it.

- **What android.24-28 actually shipped, and what this fixes.** Every build since android.24 carried the batched terrain draw - one multi-draw indirect call per run of sections instead of one call per section - and every build since android.26 disabled it on Adreno 640, because the four-record probe this renderer runs at device creation proved that the driver accepts a non-zero `firstInstance` in an indirect record and then does not fetch the record it names. Your android.28 log says it plainly: "the first-instance probe did not read its sentinels back in order, and the terrain pass will not batch on this driver" - so the terrain kept drawing one section at a time, over a thousand calls a frame, and the 10% you measured came from the arena and core-pinning fixes alone. The batching itself never ran.
- **The record now travels in the indices.** A draw needs its section's position and its vertex range; all three previous channels for that - a storage binding indexed by `instance_index`, then an instance-step attribute offset by `first_instance` - died on the same driver. The one channel nothing can refuse is the index buffer itself: every baked index now carries the section's record slot in its high bits (`(slot << 17) | vertex`), and the vertex stage reads the record out of a per-bake table through those bits. The indirect record needs no per-draw data at all any more - `first_instance` and `base_vertex` are zero in every record, on every path, on every driver.
- **Per-frame record uploads are gone.** The records used to be rebuilt and re-uploaded for every visible section every frame (hundreds of kilobytes); they are written once per bake now, and the only per-frame upload left is the indirect argument list itself. The camera-relative offset the records used to carry is three integer subtractions in the shader.
- **The probe survives, and it guards the right thing.** The game's own repeated draws (entities, block entities) still batch through `first_instance`, so the probe now gates only that path: on a driver like this one the terrain batches and the game path draws one at a time - correct on both sides, and the terrain is the part that was slow.

Expected effect on the device the last log came from: the terrain pass goes from roughly a thousand draw calls a frame back to a handful of multi-draw calls, on top of the arena and core-pinning gains already measured. If geometry appears in the wrong place or the world draws hollow - the two signatures the old driver bug produced - send the log immediately; this build changes how every terrain vertex finds its section, and a wrong constant there is visible rather than subtle.

26.1.2612.0.8-android.42:
The terrain draws straight out of the arena, and the phone presents every frame it makes.

- **The gathering now prefers drawing in place.** The compacted draw - the shape every probe-refusing device runs - merges the frame's sections into contiguous runs, and then *copies* their index ranges into a per-frame buffer to draw them as one call. But a run that is already contiguous where it lives needs no copy at all: it is one plain `draw_indexed` over its own slice of the arena. That shape is the first choice now, the compacted draw (and its 16 MB buffers, which the logs watched grow 1 -> 2 -> 4 -> 8 -> 16 MB per slot) only takes over when a pass fragments past 256 runs, and a once-a-second line names any pass that crosses. While moving - exactly when the copies used to land every frame - the blit bytes are gone, on every GPU, both vendors included.
- **vsync defaults off now** (the same defaults migration that carried the batching switch onto older configs, revision 2). Fifo, what vsync asks for, is a double-buffered queue: a frame that misses the display's refresh waits for the *next* one, so a GPU rendering at 45 fps presents at 30 - which reads as half the framerate the hardware should manage. The devices whose configs carry the old default get it flipped once; turning vsync back on holds from there. If a device still feels below its hardware after this update, check this switch first.
- The batching probes print their evidence. Both probes - first-instance and index-record - have been failing on Adreno 640 *and* Mali-G610, which is two vendors answering one question the same wrong way and no log line saying what any of them saw. A failed probe now prints the four words it read back: a collapsed call reads 100 four times, a dead fetch zeros, an unrun one the clear colour - and the next log names which of these it is, or something new.
